newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - July 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan purchased half a million tons of wheat mainly from Australia and U.S. suppliers worth $76.6 million in open bidding held at the Pakistan Embassy in Washington on Monday.

- The leader of the opposition Benazir Bhutto was stopped from taking a flight to London by the Federal Investigation Agency at the Karachi Airport. After two hours she was finally allowed to leave on another flight.
- Minister for petroleum and natural resources Chaudhry Nisar Ali Khan denied that Pakistan has offered surplus electricity to India.
- Pakistan approved $8.0 million credit line for the supply of sugar machinery to other countries from the state-run Heavy Mechanical Complex.

- The private Kohinoor Energy Ltd has served default notices to the state-run Water and Power development Authority (WAPDA) and the government of Pakistan initiating proceedings for the termination of its power purchase agreement with WAPDA.
- The average delay in shipment of goods from Pakistan due to power breakdowns has reached between 40 to 50 days causing negative impact on both exports and exporters.
- The state-run Ghee Corporation of Pakistan again postponed the domestic sale of 493 metric tonnes of RBD palm oil through open auction for an indefinite period.
- The state-run Karachi Electric Supply is likely to be privatised by end of October.
- The state's Corporate Law Authority has allowed Engro Chemical Ltd to make equity investment of one billion rupees in an associated company - Engro Asahi Polymer and Chemical Ltd.
- At least 33 people including women and children were killed and several houses collapsed in different parts of the country because of heavy monsoon rains.
- Eight employees of Water and Power Development Authority were killed and four wounded when their vehicle collided with a mini-bus coming from opposite direction.
- The federal government has decided to constitute a committee to propose amendments to the constitution.
- Nawaz Sharif will leave on a four-day official visit to Malaysia with a 70-member delegation of businessmen and traders on Thursday.
